Employees in progressions including Apprentice Meat Cutters shall receive progression increases during the life of the Agreement; however, there shall be no change in these progression.rates for the life of the Agreement.
(1) A lump sum payment will be made on 11-18-84 to non-probationary full-time (40 hour) employees in the following classifications:
Head Meat Cutters $2,500
Journeyman Meat Cutters 2,500
“Thereafter” Wrapper 2,000
Other employees in the above classifications (Head Meat Cutter, Journeyman Meat Cutter and Weighers and Wrappers “Thereafter” only) will receive a pro rata amount based on average hours worked in the preceding twelve (12) months.
It is understood pro rata lump sum for employees on an approved leave of absence and/or layoff on November 18, 1984, will be computed beginning on November 18, 1984, based on a total of 104 weeks and reduced by the amount of weeks missed. (Example, an employee is absent 20 weeks during the period beginning November 18, 1984. Upon return to work, that employee would receive a lump sum computed on 84/104 of the lump sum.)
Any employee now receiving an hourly rate above the minimum rate specified herein shall not have such rate reduced by the present Employer except as provided in Seafood Department.
* Red circle present Seafood Clerks who elect to remain in the Seafood Department as otherwise provided in this Agreement. Red circled employees will remain at their current rate of pay until such time as they would receive an increase within the Seafood rate scale.

November 20, 1983
Mr. Dale Hoagland, President
UFCW Local No. 408
Dear Mr. Hoagland:
This Letter of Agreement shall be attached to and become a part of the Agreement between United Food and Commercial Workers, Local Union No. 408 and The Kroger Co., Houston, Texas, effective November 20, 1983, through November 22, 1986.

CLARIFICATION OF ARTICLE X, SECTION N
It is agreed between the parties that when a full-time employee’s hours are reduced to less than forty (40) but not less than thirty-two (32) hours per week, the employee will have the option of exercising their seniority to the least senior full-time position by classification in the zone (district) or the employee may remain at the store for an indefinite time working the reduced schedule.
If the employee elects to remain at the store working at least thirty-two (32) but less than forty (40) hours per week and at a later time decides to exercise their seniority, the employee must notify their store manager in writing by Wednesday noon for the following week’s schedule.
A full-time employee whose hours are reduced to less than thirty-two (32) hours per week must exercise their seniority to “bump” the least senior full-time employee in their classification in their seniority area or forfeit their full-time seniority and take the part-time job in the store. Such refusal shall be in writing.
It is understood that a full-time employee’s option to remain at their store working less than forty (40) hours but not less than thirty-two (32) hours per week will waive that employee’s right to file a time claim.

ARTICLE XVII
FAVORED NATIONS
Article XVII, Favored Nations Clause of the Agreement will not apply to newly organized companies during the term of their first (1st) collective bargaining agreement (not to exceed a maximum of three (3) years), or companies that are in bankrupt status so long as such company remains in such status.

ARTICLE VII
VACATIONS
A full-time employee who is reduced to part-time because of reduction in work hours by the Employer shall retain multiple weeks of vacation earned (if any) on a pro-rata basis determined by dividing total hours worked in the vacation qualifying year by 52.
Effective November 16, 1980, part-time employees who become full-time after that date, shall have all service from date of hire considered when calculating vacation eligibility.
If you concur in the above, please indicate by signing in the space provided below.

Sincerely,
G. Donald Summers
Director - Labor Relations
Southwest
